title: Add to a Whole Range, Ask About One Cell

concept.title: Store the differences between neighbours: a range addition changes two of them, and a cell is a prefix sum of the differences
body: Now the operations **add a number to a whole range** of cells, and the questions ask for the **value of one cell**. For the row `1 1 1 1` and the operation "add 5 to the cells 2 to 3" the row becomes `1 6 6 1`, so a question about the cell 3 returns 6. Changing every cell of the range would cost O(n) per operation.

Use the **difference array**: `d[i] = a[i] - a[i-1]`. Adding `z` to all the cells from `x` to `y` changes just **two differences**: `d[x]` grows by `z` and `d[y + 1]` shrinks by `z`. The value of a cell is recovered as the sum of the differences before it: `a[i] = d[1] + d[2] + ... + d[i]`, a **prefix sum**. If the differences live in a Fenwick tree, both parts take O(log n): two point additions for an update and one prefix sum for a question.

The tree starts with zeros, and the original values are added at the end (`a0[x - 1]`), so there is no need to build differences of the input. The position `y + 1` can be `n + 1`; the tree ignores it (it only matters for cells to the right of `y`, and there are none). The complexity is O((n + q) log n). This "range update, point query" structure is the Fenwick form of the difference array used for offline range updates.

statement: A row of `n` numbers is given. Process `q` operations: type 1 `x y z` adds `z` to every number at the positions `x` to `y`; type 2 `x 0 0` asks for the current number at the position `x`. Print the answers to all the questions of type 2 on one line, in order.
inputFormat: The first line has `n` and `q`: the number of cells and the number of operations.
The second line has `n` numbers: the cells.
Each of the next `q` lines has four numbers `t`, `x`, `y` and `z`. If `t = 1`, add `z` to every cell from `x` to `y`. If `t = 2`, print the value of the cell number `x` (`y` and `z` are 0).
outputFormat: Print one number for every operation of type 2, separated by spaces.
constraints: Cells are numbered from 1; for an addition 1 <= x <= y <= n.

examples.note: After adding 5 to the cells 2 and 3 the row is 1 6 6 1: 6 1.

hints: A range addition changes only two differences.
The value of a cell is its starting value plus the prefix sum of the differences.
Keep the differences in a Fenwick tree.

explanation: The differences between neighbouring cells are kept in a Fenwick tree: a range addition changes two differences, and the value of a cell is its starting value plus the prefix sum of the differences.
solution.complexity: Time O((n + q) log n), space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

def bit_add(t, i, x):
    n = len(t) - 1
    while i <= n:
        t[i] += x
        i += i & -i

def bit_sum(t, i):
    s = 0
    while i > 0:
        s += t[i]
        i -= i & -i
    return s

n, q = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
ops = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(q)]

d = [0] * (n + 2)
out = []
for kind, x, y, z in ops:
    if kind == 1:
        bit_add(d, x, z)
        bit_add(d, y + 1, -z)
    else:
        out.append(a[x - 1] + bit_sum(d, x))
print(*out)
